findings.passage: “I don’t want to go into this election without a photo ID law and without cleaning up our voter rolls. This is a problem that we’ve known about and just haven’t adequately addressed,” Adams said.
findings.note: As Secretary of State-elect, speaking to a legislative committee, he says he wants a photo ID law and cleaner voter rolls before the 2020 elections. Quoted by WKMS (Ryland Barton).

findings.passage: “For two reasons that needs to be in there — one because it’s humane, and the other is because I want a version that will pass court muster. And I simply don’t think that a version of photo ID without this component would be constitutional,” Adams said.
findings.note: Explains why a photo ID bill should include free IDs for people who cannot afford them. Quoted by WKMS.
subjects: free state ID for voters without one

findings.passage: “The left think that the right are stealing elections through voter suppression, the right think that the left are stealing elections through the dead voting, through illegal immigrants voting,” Adams said.
findings.note: Describes the two sides' competing fears about elections while saying he will govern with progressive concerns in mind. Quoted by WKMS.

findings.passage: I’ve talked about how I implemented photo ID to vote, how I cleaned up the voter rolls, how I transitioned the state to paper ballots so we can audit.
findings.note: In an interview transcript (Semafor, Americana), he lists photo ID to vote among his accomplishments in a primary campaign. Date taken from the article URL.

findings.passage: “It’s a practical impossibility for a noncitizen to vote in a Kentucky election because we require ID,” Adams said.
findings.note: On the 2024 ballot amendment on citizen-only voting, he ties the photo ID requirement to preventing noncitizen voting. Quoted by WKYU.

findings.passage: “We have undertaken common sense election integrity measures to make sure that we have clean elections,” Adams said. “One of those is the first thing we implemented when I got into office in 2020 which was photo-ID to vote."
findings.note: Names photo ID to vote as his first election integrity measure. Quoted by WKYU.

findings.passage: “The notion of people coming to our polls and voting illegally is about the least of our problems,” Adams said.
findings.note: Says illegal voting is a small concern next to getting eligible people to vote. Quoted by WKYU.

findings.passage: “Kentucky law protects voters’ personal information, and I will not voluntarily commit a data breach by providing Kentuckians’ personal data to the federal bureaucracy unless a court order tells me to.”
findings.note: Statement after the February 2026 federal lawsuit over voter data; the exact statement date is not given, so the article date is used. Related to voter-roll data sharing, not ID.
subjects: voter-roll data sharing with federal government

findings.passage: While other states became lax on voter verification in 2020, Michael took Kentucky in the opposite direction. Kentucky was the only state to implement Photo ID to Vote in 2020.
findings.note: Campaign page (a statement issued under his campaign, written in the third person) listing photo ID to vote among his accomplishments; page is undated.
